Confidence 'high' means reproduced or directly read in code/data; web-sourced game-version facts are 'medium' because official sites could not be fetched from the audit environment.

findings.title: Skill base damage and level scaling are unsourced and contradict extracted data
findings.description: backend/app/game_data/skills.json and SKILL_STATS (179 skills each) are hand-calibrated. 53/54 comparable skills differ by more than 25% from the 1.4.6 extracted hit damage (median 24.6x). A per-level coefficient is applied that has no basis in the game data (150/184 skills have empty levelScaling).
findings.evidence: Fireball: forge base_damage 110 (skills.json:412-413) vs 1.4.6 extract damageSources fire 25, addedDamageScaling 1.25 (independently re-verified)
commands_used: python3 comparison of forge skills.json vs last-epoch-data/exports_json/skills.json damageSources
findings.user_impact: Every displayed DPS number is unreliable
findings.recommended_action: Source base damage and scaling from extracted damageSources behind provenance; label DPS as an estimate until then

findings.title: Data is a full season behind the live game
findings.description: Live game is 1.5.x Season 5 (launched ~2026-10-01, 1.5.1 on 10-02). The newest extraction is 1.4.6 (2026-05-06). Forge runtime data matches the ~1.4.3-era snapshot (synced 2026-04-26). 1.4.7 and 1.5 were never extracted; 1.5 skills (e.g. Radiant Lance) have 0 hits in the exports.
findings.evidence: last-epoch-data/exports_json/metadata.json; data/version.json; web patch-note search (medium confidence; official site blocked by local proxy)
findings.user_impact: Season 5 builds cannot be represented; values outdated
findings.recommended_action: 1.5.x extraction on the operator machine, then a provenance-stamped sync
findings.r1_notes: No 1.5.x extraction exists in any repository. R1 built the one-command operator extraction (scripts/r1_operator_extract.ps1) that reads version/build from the install (PlayerSettings.bundleVersion, Steam buildid); it has not run.

findings.title: Production data/ is pre-1.4.6 and cannot be reproduced by its own sync job
findings.description: Re-running scripts/sync_game_data.py against the current 1.4.6 exports in a scratch copy: 37 of 52 data/ files differ and 15 are identical. Ailments 11->143; quests 2->147; blessings change shape (pipeline.py:128-140 cannot index the new shape); passives.json has 6 Acolyte nodes absent in 1.4.6; 9 uniques and 15 set items are missing. version.json says patch unknown, synced 2026-04-26.
findings.user_impact: Planner serves stale, unversioned, non-reproducible game data
findings.recommended_action: Sync manifest (source commit + hashes) and idempotency check; resync
findings.r1_notes: Forge data/ is unchanged by R1 (R1.15). Extraction side: run manifests and a retroactive 1.4.6 provenance record now exist; the Forge sync carries upstream trust (sync_game_data.py upstream_trust). Resync/idempotency of data/ is R2.

findings.title: Affix tier values are stored at 100x scale and multi-property affixes are flattened to one stat
findings.description: Every tier value is multiplied by 100; only 32 of 387 flat-value affixes are divided back by the stat_engine heuristic. All 534 multi-property affixes keep one stat key and lose the secondary property's rolls.
findings.evidence: Added Health T1: game 5-15 vs data/items/affixes.json 500-1500 (independently re-verified); stat_engine.py:590-631 _FLAT_SCALE_STAT_KEYS heuristic
commands_used: python3 compare export tiers vs data/items/affixes.json
findings.user_impact: Wrong or missing affix stats feed every calculation
findings.recommended_action: Explicit value-scale contract per property/modifier type; carry all affix properties
findings.r1_notes: exports_canonical/affixes.json keeps source-scale floats (no x100) and every property of all 534 multi-property affixes with one roll per property per tier (golden tests: Added Health T1 5-15, Strength T8 24-28). Forge still consumes the x100 legacy data (R2).

findings.title: Next deploy will most likely fail: unpinned SQLAlchemy resolves 2.1.x, whose postgresql:// driver (psycopg 3) is not installed
findings.description: requirements.txt pins flask-sqlalchemy and psycopg2-binary but not SQLAlchemy. A fresh install on Python 3.11 gets SQLAlchemy 2.1.3; create_app('production') and 'flask db upgrade' raise ModuleNotFoundError: psycopg. Render reinstalls on each build, so any forward deploy (including an importer hotfix) is blocked. Reproduced independently in three environments (consolidates SYS-18 and DB-2).
findings.evidence: py3.11 venv: SQLAlchemy 2.1.3; create_engine('postgresql://..') -> ModuleNotFoundError; requirements.txt has no SQLAlchemy line | also via SYS-18: scratch venv: SQLAlchemy 2.1.3, dialect driver 'psycopg'; 6 test errors ModuleNotFoundError psycopg; requirements.txt has no SQLAlchemy line (re-verified); config.py:15 default URL postgresql:// | also via DB-2: flask db heads with a postgresql:// URL
commands_used: python3.11 -m venv; pip install -r backend/requirements.txt; pip list
findings.user_impact: Every remediation deploy is blocked; the currently running instance is probably unaffected (UNKNOWN)
findings.recommended_action: Pin SQLAlchemy<2.1 or use postgresql+psycopg2://, plus a lock/constraints file; verify on a Render preview before anything else
findings.r0_notes: SQLAlchemy pinned to 2.0.54 and postgresql:// URLs pinned to psycopg2 (config + create_app). Verified: fresh Python 3.11 venv, production config boot, flask db heads/upgrade on PostgreSQL 16. Not yet verified on Render.

findings.title: Attribute and other flat affixes reach the stat engine at 100x
findings.description: Sync multiplies all tiers by 100. get_affix_value divides back only if the stat_key is in _FLAT_SCALE_STAT_KEYS AND the T1 midpoint is >100. Strength, Intelligence, Dexterity, Attunement, Vitality and 'Level of All Skills and Added Mana' slip through. 187 affixes have a top tier >= 1000.
findings.evidence: data/items/affixes.json Strength T1 100-100, T8 2400-2800 (re-verified); stat_engine.py:609-631 threshold logic
findings.user_impact: Attribute affixes inflated ~100x in stat calculations and display
findings.recommended_action: Scale per modifier type from the export; remove the heuristic; golden tests
findings.r1_notes: Canonical affixes carry source scale; the Forge stat_engine heuristic and x100 data are unchanged until R2 consumes the canonical model.

findings.title: Sync mislabels the mastery on 190 of 541 passive nodes (index-to-name map swapped)
findings.description: MASTERY_MAP assumes Mage [Sorcerer, Runemaster, Spellblade], Primalist [Shaman, Beastmaster, Druid] and Sentinel [Paladin, Forge Guard, Void Knight]. The 1.4.6 export orders them Mage [Sorcerer, Spellblade, Runemaster], Primalist [Beastmaster, Shaman, Druid] and Sentinel [Void Knight, Forge Guard, Paladin]. /api/passives filtered by mastery returns the wrong nodes for 6 of 15 masteries. The v2 bundle and the frontend tree data are correct.
findings.evidence: scripts/sync_game_data.py:324-330 vs exports_json/classes.json masteryNames (re-verified); data/classes/passives.json mg_32 'Arcane Warden' labelled Runemaster
commands_used: python3 compare passives mastery vs export masteryNames
findings.user_impact: Wrong passive nodes and bonuses per mastery
findings.recommended_action: Derive mastery names from the export; regenerate and reseed; add a mastery-label test

findings.title: Unauthenticated PATCH rewrites the production affix data file
findings.description: PATCH /api/admin/affixes/<id> is decorated only with a rate limit (30/min) and writes data/items/affixes.json via _save_affixes. The SPA route /affixes (AffixEditorPage) calls it. Anyone can change affix tiers/stat keys used by calculations on that instance until the next deploy. Additionally, POST /api/load/game-data (no auth) hot-reloads the tampered file into the live pipeline; reproduced with the Flask test client against a scratch copy (anonymous PATCH -> 200).
findings.evidence: backend/app/routes/admin.py:68-90 (independently re-verified: no auth decorator, json.dump to AFFIXES_PATH); App.tsx:232; AffixEditorPage.tsx:363 | also via API-1: Test client: anonymous PATCH -> 200, scratch copy renamed to AUDIT-TAMPER | also via FE-6: AffixEditorPage.tsx:363
commands_used: scratchpad admin_test.py (Flask test client, scratch data copy)
findings.user_impact: Anonymous tampering with game data served to all users
findings.recommended_action: Require admin auth or disable in production; treat runtime data as read-only
findings.r0_notes: PATCH /api/admin/affixes/<id> returns 404 unless GAME_DATA_MUTATION_ENABLED (hard-coded off in ProductionConfig), then 401/403 for non-admins. Tests assert file hash and in-memory pipeline unchanged.

findings.title: Unbounded multi-target simulation allows a single-request memory DoS
findings.description: No upper bounds on max_duration, tick_size or target count; every damage event is returned.
findings.evidence: 3600s / 0.01 tick / 10 targets: 17.3s and 1.66GB RSS; a larger input was SIGKILLed
findings.user_impact: One anonymous request can OOM an instance
findings.recommended_action: Schema bounds and a response size cap
findings.r0_notes: Schema bounds (duration <=300 s, tick 0.01-10 s, <=20 targets, step budget 120,000) checked before simulation; response capped at 5,000 events with explicit truncation fields. Audit payload rejected before the engine runs.

findings.title: v2 endpoints re-parse multi-MB bundles on every request and are now linked from public pages
findings.description: 76 ungated, unauthenticated rules (41 duplicated by a double mount) reload JSON from disk on each call.
findings.evidence: modifiers/debug ~2.6s and +135MB per call; 2 concurrent calls peaked at 384MB
findings.user_impact: Slow pages; memory pressure on starter instances
findings.recommended_action: Per-process caching or env gate; remove the duplicate mount

findings.title: IDOR: anyone can change skill node allocations on any build
findings.description: PATCH /api/builds/<slug>/skills/<id>/nodes/<n> has no auth and no owner check.
findings.evidence: backend/app/routes/skills.py:281-296 (re-verified: only @limiter); anonymous PATCH on another user's private build -> 200 | also via SEC-2: backend/app/routes/skills.py:281-360
findings.recommended_action: Require owner auth
findings.r0_notes: Skill-node PATCH requires the build owner via app/services/build_access.py.

findings.title: Anonymous builds and craft sessions can be modified or deleted by others
findings.description: Anyone can PATCH anonymous builds; any logged-in user can DELETE them. The same applies to anonymous craft sessions.
findings.recommended_action: Edit token or immutable anonymous records
findings.r0_notes: Builds: only owners may update/delete; ownerless builds are read-only. Craft sessions: owned sessions owner-only (unchanged), ownerless sessions can no longer be deleted. Residual by design: ownerless craft-session action/undo still works for whoever holds the 64-bit random slug (the anonymous crafting feature depends on it); permanent anonymous lifecycle deferred to AUDIT-R4.

findings.title: Private builds readable by guessable slug
findings.description: get, simulate, skills, optimize, analysis and compare ignore is_public (only /report checks it). Imported builds are forced private, and slugs derive from the build name.
findings.evidence: anonymous GET, simulate and skills -> 200; report -> 403
findings.recommended_action: Central visibility check; random slugs
findings.r0_notes: Private owned builds readable only by the owner on every build-by-slug route (404 otherwise), checked before caches. Residual by design: ownerless builds are readable by link; new private ownerless builds get an unguessable slug, existing ones keep their slugs (AUDIT-R4).

findings.title: No ProxyFix: rate limits are likely keyed on the Render proxy IP
findings.description: remote_addr is used everywhere with no X-Forwarded-For handling.
findings.evidence: grep finds no ProxyFix or X-Forwarded
findings.user_impact: Possible sitewide shared 429s; per-client limits ineffective
findings.recommended_action: Verify with production logs; ProxyFix(x_for=1)

findings.title: Minion DPS computed from player stats while docs claim 0
findings.description: Summon Wolf shows 343 DPS; minion_* stats are unused.
findings.recommended_action: Return an unsupported status for minion skills

findings.title: Encounter-build damage treats 'more' as additive
findings.description: build_stats_engine.to_encounter_params sums the more multipliers and all damage-type pools.
findings.user_impact: Encounter DPS inconsistent with main DPS
findings.recommended_action: Reuse a single DPS pipeline

findings.title: Specialization-tree modifiers and conversions dropped on user-facing paths
findings.description: SimulateBuildSchema has no spec_tree; analyze_build passes no conversions.
findings.recommended_action: Wire spec_tree and conversions; add a route-level test

findings.title: DPS and EHP outputs carry no trust or provenance labels
findings.description: Responses have no trust, provenance or confidence fields; trust badges appear only on informational pages.
findings.recommended_action: Add a per-metric trust label and render it

findings.title: Added damage effectiveness defaults to 1.0 for 175/179 skills
findings.description: 34/56 comparable skills disagree with extracted addedDamageScaling.
findings.recommended_action: Load addedDamageScaling from extracted data

findings.title: Bleed and Ignite constants contradict the extract; data/combat/ailments.json is never read
findings.description: Bleed 43/4s vs extract 53/3s; Ignite 3.0s vs 2.5s. Electrify, Frostbite, Damned and Time Rot are excluded.
findings.recommended_action: Source ailment constants from extracted data

findings.title: Nine divergent armor mitigation implementations
findings.description: Divisors 300 / 1000 / 10*area level; caps 0.80 / 0.85 / 0.595; three different rules for non-physical damage.
findings.evidence: probe: defense_engine 50% vs calculator 41% for the same elemental hit
findings.user_impact: EHP overstated; numbers inconsistent between pages
findings.recommended_action: Single authoritative implementation pinned to a sourced formula

findings.title: Three incompatible penetration semantics; main DPS applies no enemy mitigation
findings.description: Penetration is subtracted before the cap in one implementation, floored at 0 in another; boss uses min(resistances). calculate_dps_vs_enemy has no caller.
findings.evidence: pen 30 vs res 20: calculator 0 vs domain -10
findings.user_impact: Penetration affixes are worthless in main DPS
findings.recommended_action: Unify semantics; verify against a sourced mechanic

findings.title: Fabricated mastery and keystone bonuses plus a modulo passive fallback
findings.description: Unknown keystones get spell +10 / hp +50; /simulate/build cycles stats by modulo when passive_tree is omitted.
findings.user_impact: Invented stats inflate DPS and EHP
findings.recommended_action: Remove or flag fallbacks; surface a data-gap field

findings.title: 'Increased Armor' affix is added as flat armour
findings.description: stat_key 'armour': a T5 roll gives +29 flat instead of +29%.
findings.recommended_action: Map to armour_pct; add a test

findings.title: Ward decay formula appears outdated
findings.description: Uses 0.4W/(1+0.5R); community/dev-notes formula is (0.2W+0.00005W^2)/(1+0.5R). The INT retention constant differs between modules (4 vs 2).
findings.recommended_action: Verify against an official source; pin to patch

findings.title: Deleting any build that has been viewed fails with HTTP 500
findings.description: The BuildView backref has no cascade, so the ORM nulls a NOT NULL foreign key on delete.
findings.evidence: models/__init__.py:361 backref('views') with no cascade (re-verified); IntegrityError NOT NULL build_views.build_id in a scratch DB
findings.recommended_action: cascade + ON DELETE CASCADE via a new migration
findings.r0_notes: ORM cascade + ON DELETE CASCADE (migration a7c3e91f4d20). Reproduced 500 on PostgreSQL 16 before; 204 after; raw SQL cascade verified.

findings.title: Saved builds carry no data-version stamp; patch_version is stale client-supplied text
findings.description: patch_version defaults to 1.2.1; the pipeline version is 'unknown'; passive IDs were recreated (int to str) and are pruned on reseed.
findings.user_impact: Saved builds cannot be reliably reinterpreted after a patch
findings.recommended_action: Server-set data_version and patch columns

findings.title: Several non-runtime combat simulators exist beside the live path
findings.description: The live path is simulation_service + stat/combat/defense engines. Others (app/engines/combat_simulator, app/combat, app/domain/fight_simulator, backend/combat, backend/simulation) are test-only or orphaned.
findings.user_impact: Fixes and validation may target the wrong engine
findings.recommended_action: Declare the canonical engine; label the rest

findings.title: Four affix data paths; the legacy file is read directly by multiple modules
findings.description: Legacy affixes.json is read by affix_engine, the pipeline, stat_engine, the importer and others; the forge-safe and v2 paths are off by default.
findings.recommended_action: One selection service

findings.title: Release readiness claims omit a red frontend suite
findings.description: 17 vitest failures; the release doc reports only focused subsets.
findings.recommended_action: Report the full suite in release gates

findings.title: Docs claim patch 1.4.3 from version.json, which says 'unknown'
findings.description: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS cites data/version.json as the source of the 1.4.3 claim.
findings.recommended_action: Single version source

findings.title: 'Users can rely on trusted data' contradicts upstream trusted_public_visibility_ready=false
findings.description: The trust vocabularies in the two repos conflict.
findings.recommended_action: Shared glossary plus an explicit exposure decision

findings.title: API reference labels unauthenticated writes as 'Admin'; 89 routes undocumented
findings.description: All 77 documented paths exist; 6 stable and 83 experimental rules are missing from the reference.
findings.user_impact: Implies protection that does not exist
findings.recommended_action: Document actual auth

findings.title: Forge runtime data was never synced to 1.4.6
findings.description: A replay of the sync transform shows the Forge affixes match 1.4.3-era extractor commits. 1.4.6 adds 3 affixes and changes 16 tier records (e.g. idol minion penetration T1 1-2 vs 3-4). Uniques 403 vs 409; set items 47 vs 59.
commands_used: python3 -I sync_game_data.py --affixes (scratch root, per extractor commit)
findings.user_impact: Wrong values; missing affixes and uniques
findings.recommended_action: Re-sync with source commit and hash recorded
findings.r1_notes: Not changed by R1.

findings.title: Patch identity inconsistent across surfaces
findings.description: /api/health returns 'unknown'; /api/version hard-codes 1.4.3 / season 4; builds default to patch 1.2.1; seed builds are 1.4.3 with cycle 1.2; v2 bundles carry a SHA only.
findings.recommended_action: Single provenance source from extractor metadata

findings.title: Fresh extraction is only possible on one Windows operator machine
findings.description: Requires the game install (D:\, Steam registry), Il2CppDumper/AssetRipper .exe, .NET, UnityPy and pythonnet. There is no 1.4.6 or 1.5 snapshot in patch_versions.
findings.user_impact: Patch response depends on one machine and one operator
findings.recommended_action: Document and archive per-patch snapshots; CI-runnable post-processing subset

findings.title: No gating patch-diff, schema-drift or unknown-enum detection
findings.description: validate_exports checks shrinkage, minimum counts, top-level keys and duplicate IDs only; additions and value changes pass. The unknown-value validator (148 unknowns) is not wired into run_all.
findings.evidence: validate_exports exit 0; tag validator reports 148 unknowns
findings.recommended_action: Gating patch-diff and unknown-field/enum report

findings.title: Semantic coverage is 0%: no v2 record is stable-calculable, and there are no ground-truth fixtures
findings.description: Of 8,711 records across the v2 bundles, 0 are classified as stable-calculable. Skill nodes reaching the production resolver: 2,186 of 3,783 allocatable (57.8%). Actors: 239 of 1,020 (23.4%). Skill-to-class: 60 of 184 (32.6%).
findings.recommended_action: Define semantic certification with in-game ground truth
findings.r1_notes: Semantic coverage reported separately as 0 in R1_COVERAGE_METRICS.json; never mixed into extraction completeness. Ground-truth fixtures remain future work.

findings.title: Core simulation inputs are hand-authored or third-party, not extracted
findings.description: backend/app/game_data/{skills,classes,constants}.json, base_items, crafting rules, FP ranges, rarities and enemy_profiles are hand-authored. The weaver tree is scraped from a third-party planner (game 1.4.2). Only 17 of 115 curated base items exist in 1.4.6, and 17 of the 179 hand-authored skill entries match no 1.4.6 skill.
findings.user_impact: Unverified data presented as game data
findings.recommended_action: Provenance label per family; replace with extracted data
findings.r1_notes: r1_forge_consumption_inventory lists 10 non-extracted runtime inputs (base_items, weaver_tree, enemy_profiles, crafting_rules, ...) and hand-authored backend game_data files. Replacement is R2.

findings.title: 19 game data tables present in the 1.4.6 resources manifest are never extracted; weaver tree decoded then dropped
findings.description: Never extracted: factions, constellations/prophecies, woven echoes, champions, arena, shrines, memories, harbingers/tombs/omens, corruption config, idol altar properties, crafting materials, property definitions, caches/rewards. The 77-node weaver tree is decoded and then dropped.
findings.evidence: extracted_raw/resources_manifest.json by_script vs grep of exports
findings.user_impact: Whole systems unmodelled; completeness claims overstated
findings.recommended_action: Enumeration-based coverage gate against the game's own table manifest
findings.r1_notes: Generated denominator (1,326 candidates from all 1,170 manifest classes + secondary sources) rediscovers every listed family mechanically and classifies it; raw TypeTree dumps + lossless canonical envelopes for every in-scope class run in the operator extraction. Weaver tree now survives (exports_canonical/weaver_tree.json, 77 nodes, all prerequisites resolved; R1.15 flags 18 legacy-decoder field-shift nodes). Correction: MaterialList is a rendering-material table by its il2cpp layout, not crafting materials. R1.15: UNKNOWN reduced 744 -> 399 by evidence-based structural rules; 581 extraction contracts declare what the operator run must dump.

findings.title: 1.4.6 raw inputs are absent and some exports have no writer
findings.description: No 1.4.6 game files or raw_bundles are in the repo. actors.json has had no writer since commit 66c6498. Loot and monster-mod processors read uncommitted inputs.
findings.user_impact: Exports cannot be regenerated or audited
findings.recommended_action: Hashed raw snapshot archive (outside git if needed) plus a run manifest
findings.r1_notes: Raw snapshot contract implemented (r1_snapshot.py: every install file hashed, extraction inputs in a content store outside git, committed manifests). No snapshot exists yet; retroactive 1.4.6 record states reproducible_from_raw=false.

findings.title: Committed render.yaml sets VITE_API_BASE_URL without /api; a build from the blueprint would 404 every API call and break Discord login
findings.description: lib/api.ts composes `${BASE_URL}${path}` with /api-relative paths (/builds, /auth/me). render.yaml:95-96 sets https://api.epochforge.gg, while every backend blueprint is mounted under /api. A build with that value contains https://api.epochforge.gg/auth/discord. However, the 403 incident proves production reached /api/import/build, so production's actual value must differ from the blueprint (likely a dashboard override). This is undocumented config drift: re-applying the blueprint would break the whole app.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/api.ts:51-54,88 (re-verified); render.yaml:95-96; prod-config scratch build + Playwright logged un-prefixed requests; the Discord alert proves the live backend received /api/import/build
findings.user_impact: Latent full outage on the next blueprint sync; live value UNKNOWN
findings.recommended_action: Read the live Render env value; make render.yaml match it; add a URL-composition test
findings.r0_notes: Repository is internally correct: any VITE_API_BASE_URL form composes to /api/... (verified in Chromium with the committed render.yaml value). The live Render dashboard value was not readable from this environment and requires operator verification; not VERIFIED.

findings.title: v2 trust/debug pages fetch root-relative paths that cannot work on the static host
findings.description: Eight public routes fetch /experimental/v2/* or /api/experimental/* from the frontend origin. The static SPA rewrite returns index.html, so the page shows 'Backend returned an unreadable response (200)'.
findings.evidence: Observed on /debug/v2-skills and /debug/v2-stats-modifiers in a local prod-config build
findings.recommended_action: Route through the API base; test

findings.title: Importer dead ends: Maxroll 403 shown as expiry, LET URL accepted in URL tab, Quick Fetch permanently disabled, 'issue reported' footer never renders
findings.description: The 403 message blames expiry or format. The JSON tab cannot take Maxroll data. The footer checks for the string '422', which backend messages never contain.
findings.recommended_action: Detect 403s and route users to the paste/bookmarklet path
findings.r0_notes: Partially addressed in R0: LET URLs routed to the JSON flow; Maxroll 403 no longer described as an expired build. Remaining for AUDIT-R4: Quick Fetch tab still shown (disabled), the '422' issue-reported footer never renders, no paste fallback for Maxroll.

findings.title: Anonymous and imported builds cannot be edited, published or shared in the UI
findings.description: isOwner requires an author; there is no is_public control; imports are forced private; there is no share button; /workspace has no save path. The backend allows anyone to PATCH an anonymous build (an ownership-model gap).
findings.evidence: BuildPlannerPage isOwner logic; import_route forces is_public=False
findings.recommended_action: Define an anonymous ownership model; add publish and share controls

findings.title: Default Import URL tab still routes LE Tools URLs to the dead server-side fetch
findings.description: handleFullImport rejects only unknown sources. The LE Tools 'use JSON tab' text is just a hint and the button stays enabled, so the backend fetches, gets a 403 and fires a hard alert every time.
findings.evidence: BuildImportModal.tsx:86-95,263-289,304-317; the repo itself says the server-side fetch is dead (import_route.py:432-434)
findings.user_impact: Users see a raw 'HTTP 403' with no pointer to the bookmarklet; the alert channel fills with noise

findings.r0_notes: LET planner URLs are never submitted to the server importer; the modal routes to the JSON/bookmarklet flow with the original URL preserved.

findings.title: Server-side LE Tools fetch gets HTTP 403 from production, and nothing is logged that would identify the source
findings.description: A single requests.get with a hard-coded Chrome/120 User-Agent and no retries. Only the status integer is logged. No server, cf-ray or cf-mitigated header and no body snippet is captured, so a Cloudflare 403 cannot be told apart from an origin 403.
findings.evidence: lastepochtools_importer.py:693-727; the local egress proxy blocked live observation
findings.user_impact: LE Tools URL import is non-functional in production (per incident)
findings.recommended_action: Treat server-side fetch as unsupported; if it is kept, capture upstream diagnostic headers. Do not evade upstream protection
findings.r0_notes: Server-side LET fetch retired (/api/import/build and /api/import/url return 422 LET_SERVER_FETCH_UNSUPPORTED, no fetch, no alert). Importers now record HTTP status and safe upstream headers. Upstream LE Tools behaviour itself is unchanged and not bypassed.

findings.title: Raw affix dump reads uint8 SP property ids as signed bytes

findings.recommended_action: Normalize by declared field type in the raw dumper; canonical builder already corrects and records it
findings.r1_notes: Found during AUDIT-R1 (2026-10-06).

findings.title: Skill-tree walker misses six Acolyte nodes, decodes garbage prerequisites and never decodes structured node stats
findings.description: extract_skill_trees_fast.py failed 11 nodes (6 AcolyteTree = the audit's 'Forge-only' ids 86,88,97,98,101,103); every class tree has misread prerequisite pathIds (e.g. 1684808296038400); SkillTreeNode.nodeStats and propertiesForAltText are never decoded, only tooltip text.
findings.recommended_action: Decode SkillTreeNode from the il2cpp-declared layout against real 1.5 bytes; keep the canonical integrity gates
findings.r1_notes: Found during AUDIT-R1 (2026-10-06). R1.15 root cause, proven from the committed 1.4.6 dump: the walker never read SkillTreeNode.nodeStats. It read one u32 where the layout serializes two list counts and hid the shift with peek heuristics (185/185 empty-stats nodes have their description in altText). The strict layout-ordered decoder (last-epoch-data 02e4b34) fails nodes with a non-empty nodeStats loudly (NODE_STATS_LAYOUT_UNKNOWN). The operator TypeTree dump of every *TreeNode is the lossless source; the six Acolyte ids have a regression gate.

findings.r1_notes: Found during AUDIT-R1 (2026-10-06).

findings.title: The pipeline does not re-run Il2CppDumper on a new patch
